key_insight: Detecting corrupted medical-imaging inputs does not establish that removing them improves model generalization.
clinical_relevance: Medical-imaging AI curation should validate sample identity and test downstream performance rather than treat attribution anomalies as sufficient grounds for deletion.
method: Separated anomaly detection, harmfulness estimation, and intervention utility into testable claims.
Audited a 3D CTA aneurysm-candidate classifier using patient-disjoint data and preserved identifiers.
Compared full-data training with corrupted-positive removal across five paired seeds and budget-matched random-removal controls.
evidence_signal: The audit found 232 zero-valued arrays among 1,201 positive patches; removing 170 training positives yielded AUC 0.9617 versus 0.9652 with full data (difference −0.0035; 95% CI −0.0082 to 0.0007).
watch_item: Negative rank-order agreement between GradCAM++ and Integrated Gradients for positives limits method-independent anatomical interpretation.
paper_title: Leakage-Safe Auditing of Attribution-Driven Data Curation in Medical Imaging
